mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen 4.0 points week-on-week (t-1w to t-0w: -54.0 to -50.1), signaling resumption of office commuting. This sustained recovery in workplace presence over the next four weeks will drive retail-and-recreation footfall as workers return to pre-work and post-work shopping routines.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -54.0 to -50.1 in most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses by more than 3 points in any of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized near -20% after a brief dip to -16.3% (t-1w), indicating outdoor recreation demand is plateauing. This ceiling effect in parks will redirect discretionary mobility toward indoor retail-and-recreation venues as weather deteriorates and outdoor substitution becomes less attractive over the next four weeks.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -20.9 in t-0w after -16.3 in t-1w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -10% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines relative to the prior 28-day mean.

evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -56.3 to -53.9 in most recent week
failure_condition: TRANSIT reverses to below -55% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to exceed the prior 28-day mean.

candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM declines in the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not rise in at least 3 of the next 4 weeks.
